input.summary: In the parallel coordinate system, `niceScaleExtent()` is invoked inside the per-series loop, so the first contributing series' data extent gets frozen into the scale's cached `rawExtentInfo`; every subsequent `niceScaleExtent()` call then re-applies that stale extent via `scale.setExtent()`, wiping out the union performed for later series. The fix is to union the data extent across ALL contributing series first, then call `niceScaleExtent()` once per axis afterwards — matching the pattern already used by `coord/cartesian/Grid.ts` and `coord/radar/Radar.ts`. No new public option; this is a pure behavior bugfix.
steps: ROOT CAUSE (read-only confirmation, no edit needed). `/workspace/src/coord/axisHelper.ts` line 157-192 `niceScaleExtent()` calls `getScaleExtent(scale, model)` (line 162), which at line 67 calls `ensureScaleRawExtentInfo(scale, model, scale.getExtent())`. `/workspace/src/coord/scaleRawExtentInfo.ts` lines 295-313 `ensureScaleRawExtentInfo()` CACHES the result on `scale.rawExtentInfo` and returns the cached instance on every later call ('Do not permit to recreate.', line 302-306). The cached `_dataMin`/`_dataMax` come from the extent at the time of the FIRST call. `niceScaleExtent` then does `scale.setExtent(extent[0], extent[1])` (axisHelper.ts line 175), i.e. it RESETS the scale extent back to the first series' bounds. So: series #1 unions [1,5] -> rawExtentInfo cached with dataMin=1/dataMax=5; series #2 unions [1,100] -> extent becomes [1,100]; the second `niceScaleExtent` call reads the cached [1,5] and calls `setExtent(1,5)`, truncating the axis.

NO other source change is required. Verified by grep that `axisHelper.niceScaleExtent` is referenced for parallel axes only at `/workspace/src/coord/parallel/Parallel.ts:188`; nothing in `src/component/axis/ParallelAxisView.ts`, `src/component/axis/parallelAxisAction.ts`, `src/chart/parallel/*`, or `src/coord/parallel/AxisModel.ts` re-nices the scale or depends on it being niced per-series. The coordinate system (and therefore each `ParallelAxis` and its `Scale`) is recreated from scratch on every update in `/workspace/src/coord/parallel/parallelCreator.ts:37` (`new Parallel(...)`), so no explicit `scale.setExtent(Infinity, -Infinity)` reset is needed the way `Grid.ts:513` does it.

NO new public option, no `*Option` interface change, no `index.d.ts`/`package.json`/`theme/` change. `ParallelAxisOption` in `/workspace/src/coord/parallel/AxisModel.ts` (line ~48) stays as is. Existing `min`/`max`/`boundaryGap` options keep working: after the fix the `rawExtentInfo` is built once from the full multi-series data extent, so explicit `min`/`max` on a `parallelAxis` still take priority (see `ScaleRawExtentInfo.calculate()`, `/workspace/src/coord/scaleRawExtentInfo.ts:164-250`), and `min: 'dataMin'` / `max: 'dataMax'` / a `min`/`max` callback now correctly receive the extent of ALL series instead of only the first one.

ADD A REGRESSION TEST at `/workspace/test/ut/spec/coord/parallel.test.ts` (new file; the directory `test/ut/spec/coord/` does not exist yet — create it). `test/ut/jest.config.cjs` already matches `'**/spec/coord/**/*.test.ts'` (testMatch list), so no jest config change is needed. Prepend the Apache license header block copied verbatim from `/workspace/test/ut/spec/scale/interval.test.ts` lines 1-18. Follow that file's structure: `import { createChart, getECModel } from '../../core/utHelper';` and `import { EChartsType } from '@/src/echarts';` (`utHelper` imports `src/echarts.all`, so `parallel` is registered). Test body: set an option with `parallel: {}`, two `parallelAxis` entries (`{dim: 0, name: 'A'}`, `{dim: 1, name: 'B'}`), and TWO `series` of `type: 'parallel'` where the SECOND series has values well outside the first's bounds — e.g. series[0] `data: [[1, 1], [2, 2]]`, series[1] `data: [[100, 100], [200, 200]]`. Then assert the axis extent covers the second series: `const axis = (getECModel(chart).getComponent('parallelAxis', 0) as any).axis; expect(axis.scale.getExtent()[1]).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(200);` (and `[0]` <= 1). Before the fix this yields ~2; after the fix it yields >= 200. Add a symmetric case where the later series has a SMALLER minimum (e.g. series[1] contains -50) and assert `getExtent()[0] <= -50`.

OPTIONAL manual/visual check: `/workspace/test/parallel-aqi.html`, `/workspace/test/parallel-nutrients.html` and `/workspace/test/parallel-large.html` are the existing browser test pages for this coord system. A new multi-series case can be added there, but it is not required by the requirement. Do not modify existing screenshot baselines.
input.risks:
1) Behavior change for parallel components with ZERO contributing series: previously `niceScaleExtent` was never reached, leaving `scale._extent` at `[Infinity, -Infinity]` and `isBlank()` false. After the fix it is always called, which sets `scale.setBlank(true)` (axisHelper.ts:69) so no ticks/labels are drawn. The extent itself is unchanged because `getScaleExtent` returns `[NaN, NaN]` for an inverted extent (`scaleRawExtentInfo.ts:92-94`) and `Scale._innerSetExtent` (`src/scale/Scale.ts:151-159`) ignores NaN. This matches how `Grid.ts` already behaves for empty cartesian axes, so it is a fix rather than a regression — but any screenshot baseline showing a parallel chart with axes and no data may change.
2) `each(this.dimensions, ...)` in the new trailing loop must be passed `this` as the third argument (zrender's `each(arr, cb, context)`), otherwise `this._axesMap` is undefined at runtime. TypeScript will not catch this because the callback is a `function` expression.
3) Category (`type: 'category'`) parallel axes now get `niceScaleExtent` exactly once instead of N times; `OrdinalScale` extent derives from `model.getCategories().length` (`scaleRawExtentInfo.ts:133`), so this is a no-op for them, but it is worth eyeballing `test/parallel-feature.html` which mixes category and value axes.
4) The identical latent bug exists at `/workspace/src/coord/single/Single.ts:98-107` (`niceScaleExtent` inside `ecModel.eachSeries`). It is OUT OF SCOPE for this requirement — do not change it, or the diff will overreach.
5) Do not "fix" this in `ensureScaleRawExtentInfo` by allowing recreation; that cache is intentional (see the comment at `scaleRawExtentInfo.ts:280-294` about `min`/`max` callbacks not being invoked multiple times) and changing it would affect dataZoom and every other coord system.
